basis: Congenital joint contractures define a disorder of the locomotor system.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; visual impairment in 6/15 (~40%). Joint laxity alone does not establish damage; recurrent infections do not establish immunodeficiency.
Collagen VI myopathy with muscle degeneration and contractures. Isolated renal and skin reports do not establish common damaging involvement; respiratory weakness is muscular.
Single-gene diabetes defines endocrine pancreatic dysfunction; diabetic organ complications are separate diseases.
Syndrome defined by cerebral abnormalities, renal abnormalities and digital malformations; sparse supplied clinical detail.
Isolated developmental eye disorder with coloboma, optic disc abnormalities and impaired vision.
Autoimmune necrotizing vasculitis; destructive skin lesions in ~75% and peripheral neuropathy in ~40-50%. Underlying rheumatoid arthritis is a separate disease.
Rod-cone retinal dystrophy with visual field loss in all reported patients; neurologic findings occur in only 1/61.
Craniosynostosis and intellectual disability are the defining skeletal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities.
Malignant muscle neoplasm classified under musculoskeletal system cancer; no specific visceral organ of origin is given.
Necrotizing vasculitis; cutaneous involvement 80-99%, neuropathy 30-79%. Renal involvement also 30-79%, omitted at cap; gastrointestinal involvement only 5-29%.
Infection directly inflames and damages the corneal epithelium.
Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes. HPV association does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Corpus callosum maldevelopment and pituitary hormone deficiency define the syndrome.
Hereditary spastic paraplegia; pes cavus in 5/8 and skeletal muscle atrophy in 30-79%. Bladder dysfunction occurs in fewer than 30%.
Inherited skin fragility with progressive acral-to-truncal blistering; common damaging extracutaneous involvement is not established for this subtype.
Supplied phenotype establishes retinal disease: visual impairment in 15/16, tritanomaly in 15/15 and retinal thinning in 5/16.
Craniosynostosis, syndactyly, ptosis and strabismus define disease. Hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%; external ear shape alone does not establish functional damage.
Lysosomal ceramide disorder; destructive arthropathy in Farber disease or muscle wasting in SMA affects most. Neurologic, skin and airway involvement varies across subtypes.
Branchiootorenal syndrome is defined by ear/hearing and renal developmental abnormalities; hearing impairment 4/4 and renal dysplasia 2/4.
Disorder of the inner ear labyrinth and vestibular function.
Squamous carcinoma originates in skin of the external ear, covering both the cutaneous tissue and named ear site.
Complex congenital heart malformation; pulmonary stenosis concerns cardiovascular outflow. Heterotaxy alone does not establish other organ dysfunction.
Primary cutaneous CD30-positive T-cell lymphoproliferation within the cutaneous lymphoma spectrum. Later associated lymphomas are separate diseases.
Developmental disability and skeletal malformations define syndrome; vesicoureteral reflux and cleft palate each occur in 30-79%. Heart abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
